name: OrioleDB
tagline: Cloud-native storage engine for PostgreSQL with undo logs, no VACUUM bloat and row-level WAL.
description: OrioleDB is a table access method for PostgreSQL that replaces the heap with an index-organized, copy-on-write design: undo logs instead of dead tuples, page-level compression, lock-free in-memory page access and row-level WAL that suits replication and S3-backed storage. It aims to fix Postgres' classic pain points (VACUUM, bloat, buffer contention, write amplification) without forking the SQL layer, though today it still requires a set of patches to PostgreSQL 17 that are being upstreamed. Supabase acquired the project in 2024 and launched it as a public beta on Supabase in October 2026, explicitly not yet recommended for production.

pricing.notes: Open source; available on Supabase paid plans as a public beta.

scale.notes: Single-primary Postgres scaling; experimental S3 mode decouples storage.

strengths: Undo-log MVCC eliminates table bloat and routine VACUUM
Index-organized tables with page-level compression cut storage
Lock-free page access scales better on many-core machines
Row-level WAL reduces write amplification and enables S3-native storage
Keeps full PostgreSQL SQL and extension compatibility at the query layer
weaknesses: Still beta; not recommended for production by its own maintainers
Requires a patched PostgreSQL build rather than stock Postgres
Some index types and features are not yet supported on OrioleDB tables
useCases: Write-heavy Postgres OLTP suffering from bloat
Evaluating next-generation Postgres storage on Supabase
High-concurrency workloads on large multi-core servers
notIdealFor: Production systems needing proven stability today
Managed Postgres services other than Supabase
Workloads relying on unsupported index access methods
